about: What of a note's frontmatter keyword search reads (M59.2): one rule, so the agent's search_notes and a database view's search see the same text. Properties come in frontmatter order, then relationships (wikilink fields, bracket-stripped by the scanner) in key order. A string gives its trimmed text, and a blank one gives nothing. An integer gives its digits, a float its shortest decimal (1.0 reads 1), and a boolean true or false. An array gives each item by the same rule, nested arrays included. An object or null gives nothing. A key's texts join with ", ", and a key whose texts are all empty gives no field. A key starting with _ gives nothing (the app's own bookkeeping), and so do the page chrome keys listed in chrome_keys, which equal PAGE_CHROME_KEYS in src/engine/pageChrome.ts. On an Agent record (a reserved type name, CV-08), recent, memory and preferences give nothing: an agent's memory is never searchable (D7). A title property whose text equals the note's title gives nothing, since the title is searched already. Replayed by searchable_fields_replay_the_shared_cases in src-tauri/src/search.rs and by src/engine/searchable.test.ts. `why` is for the reader.

values.why: A string is its trimmed text.
A decimal is its shortest spelling.
Null is not recorded, so there is nothing to find.
A flat array gives each item by the same rule.
A nested array is read item by item, never as one joined blob.
An object gives nothing: no [object Object], no keys.
An object inside an array gives nothing, and its siblings still count.
